title: Buying a Business? Your Forecast Won't Save the Deal

scenes.vo: Buying a business with an SBA loan? Your forecast likely can't save the deal.

captions.text: Buying a business with an SBA loan?
Your forecast likely can't save the deal.

scenes.vo: Since October first, most buyers need 1.25 times coverage from past earnings.
Every 100 dollars of loan payments needs 125 dollars of earnings.
A 500,000 dollar deal needs 50,000 down. Seller financing covers half, at most.

captions.text: Seller financing covers half, at most.

scenes.vo: Before any offer, divide last year's earnings by the payments. Under 1.25? Renegotiate.

captions.text: divide last year's earnings by the payments.

examplePayments.source: Illustrative. Earnings needed $125 and cushion $25 computed in S3How.tsx

exampleDeal.source: Illustrative, assumes total project cost equals price. $50,000 equity, $450,000 financed and $25,000 / $25,000 split computed in S4Real.tsx

notes: Coleman Report webinar blurb (2026-08-19) conflicts on projections and equity; script follows Starfield & Smith, PilieroMazza and Matthews and says 'likely'. Check SOP Appendix 15 before publishing.
'Most buyers' means initial acquisitions and owner buyouts; business expansions stay at 1.15x.
